author: cushag
text:
The day is done, and now's the night:

And all the earth may sleep, but not I;

For when each leaf has fallen from its tree,

I shall see what it was like before!

Before the sun rose red in cloudless skies,
When all the birds were flying south,
In days that came so fast we scarcely knew,
There stood a little girl with eyes as blue

As they are still—though she will never be again—

So bright that you could see them shine across the sea...

How happy I am at this news!
Please come to my home as promised,
And bring your daughter with you too;
You may well take along your wife.

author: buchanan_robert
text: In the middle of the night, the cat meowed as if grieving. The man lay awake in the dark room as usual. Suddenly he heard something move in the corner of the bedroom. He thought that it must be one of his cats waking up from its nap. But when he got out of bed to check on them, they were all asleep. After this, he went back to bed wondering what had made such noise during his sleeplessness.

author: cushag
text:
The rain is falling, and the rain will fall;

The wind is blowing, and it blows again:

We all must die, I know, but what's that to me?

For when my heart was young, life was not pain,

And love went smiling by--the rain fell then, and still

It falls upon my lonely grave-stone, yet the sun

Is shining on its flowers as before!

Ilocano is spoken by about 10 million people, and is classified as a Northern Philippine language. It belongs to the Malayo-Polynesian branch of the Austronesian languages family.[4] The name Ilocano means "of Iloko" or "belonging to Ilokos", referring to its origin from the province of Ilocos Norte. Linguists classify it along with Pangasinan (with which they share a considerable number of cognate words) as one of two major subfamilies within the Northern Philippines subgroup: Western Philippine Group and Eastern Philippine Group. author: john_keats
text:
Ah! when shall I be, and where?

What day-dreamer's ear has caught the sound of music there,
While on the sea-side wave we play, or by our garden walk
See, as they glide through air, their happy flight pursued;

When shall it come, so blest to hear its melody !

Sweet are those sounds, though mute my voice is at that time,
Or but an echo to the notes which then will chime ;
For me, if still they rise around, no more I wander far—

author: william_wordsworth
text:
The King looked down upon his people, and he saw
 A little boy—and yet it might have been an old man —

 With no hair on his head, or beard, but with some that grew from under his chin;

 And his face was like wrinkled parchment and pale brown.

 His eyes were wide open—not as if they would look out at anything, 

 But as if their lids would shut against the light.
